name: Light aubergine
lede: Light aubergine is a dark reddish purple from the Japanese traditional color system, where it stands for *murasaki*, the word for both the color purple and the murasaki root once used to dye it.

sections.title: Murasaki: a plant and a purple
sections.body:
Our graph files this swatch as a Japanese traditional color name, with the kanji 紫 and the romanized reading *murasaki*, meaning simply "purple" [1]. In Japan, the word names both the color and the plant: *murasaki* is gromwell, *Lithospermum erythrorhizon*, whose root dyed cloth this deep reddish purple before synthetic dyes replaced it [1]. The English display name links the shade to the Western vegetable aubergine, the eggplant, whose dark purple skin our library independently dates as a color word to 1794 [1][2].

In the color graph, Light aubergine's nearest named neighbor is [[coronation|Coronation]], 3.0 units away, with [[japanese-violet|Japanese Violet]] close behind at 3.4 and [[adamia|Adamia]] at 3.6 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dark purple in 8 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, as photographed, with the within-painting lens finding it in 5, rarer than 75 percent of our named colors [3]. The earliest dated match on file is a work by Giovanni Battista Paggi from 1586; that floor marks the limit of a thin early archive, not proof the shade existed earlier still, since the match is a look-alike hue in an old varnished photograph [3]. Inside the paintings that do hold it, it most often plays a shadow, in 60 percent of its matches [3].
